text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[64,128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":1.25,"footprint":1.5},"rationale":"Best observed is attempt-01 (232.89us): block_M=64, block_N=128, block_K=32, stage=2, threads=256, swizzle=8. Attempt-03 selected small block_M=32 with wide block_N=256, stage=1, swizzle=64 and regressed to 440.81us despite lower proxy cost, showing the monotone reuse proxy misranks large panels and narrow-M/wide-N choices, and that stage=1 under-pipelines. Revision: narrow swizzle to {0,4,8,16} to avoid cache-exceeding panels (32,64 dropped); require num_stages>=2 to keep K-pipelining since stage=1 hurt; add threads=64 as the early changed-thread-domain hypothesis per guidance while keeping 128/256; keep block_K up to 128 to test the untested wider-K option but retain 32 which worked. Weights: pipeline raised to 1.25 to favor deeper stages, footprint 1.5 kept since 32KB cap binds, launches 0.5 kept. block_M=32 and block_N=256 remain allowed so HiGHS can still probe them but the proxy now penalizes their narrow-M/high-launch combos. Validation scope: Metal runs exact source/TIR numerically; CUDA binaries are not executed; GB10 figures are simulator estimates, not hardware. Next hypothesis: stage in {2,3} with block_K in {32,64} and swizzle in {4,8,16} near the attempt-01 region should beat 232.89us; observe whether threads=64 helps or hurts and whether swizzle>8 materializes locality gains."}
